newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss parliament approves scaled-down mad cow cull.
newsitem.headline: Swiss parliament approves scaled-down mad cow cull.

text.p: Switzerland's parliament approved a scaled-down cull of cows on Monday that falls far short of the government's original proposal to slaughter 230,000 animals in a bid to eradicate "mad cow" disease.
A compromise bill adopted by both houses of parliament calls for culling only around 1,100 cows.
It affects animals from herds where the disease has been reported and which were born before December 1990, the year when Switzerland adopted measures to stem the disease.
In addition, herds that include any cows born after 1990 that contract the disease in future would be culled completely.
The vote was carried by the National Council, the lower house of parliament, by a 104-54 margin.

After Britain, Switzerland has the most cases of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE). It has reported 230 cases of the disease. Scientists suspect tainted beef products can trigger the brain-wasting Cruezfeldt-Jakob Disease in humans.

The coalition government proposed in September that 230,000 cows should be slaughtered to eradicate the disease in Switzerland once and for all. That programme would have cost around 320 million Swiss francs.
The latest scheme will cost only around 25 million francs.
